page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v5 is a constrained vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores operating at up to 3.525 GHz. It features 672.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 14.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include integrated support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, and AVX vector instructions, while excluding AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage is provisioned via an integrated 3865 GB solid-state drive.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel computing and memory performance. The server scored in the top 10 percent on the PassMark memory test and achieved top-quartile results in multi-core metrics, including PassMark CPU, multi-core Geekbench, and multi-core stress-ng. Multithreaded compression tests showed high throughput, reaching 221.24 GB/sec on bzip3 decompression. Large block uncached memory bandwidth delivered 106.1 GB/sec for read operations and 58.16 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, CPU-based execution of 70B parameter large language models drops to 2.35 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators and AVX-512 capabilities.

The constrained vCPU architecture offers qualitative licensing cost efficiencies by halving the active core count relative to standard 96-vCPU memory allocations while preserving the full 672.0 GB memory footprint. This makes the configuration cost-effective for enterprise software licensed on a per-core basis that requires high memory density. The instance is well suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching systems, large-scale ETL pipelines, and data analytics workloads requiring substantial fast local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing the AMD EPYC 7763 platform on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores at 3.525 GHz and couples 672.0 GB of memory with a 3865 GB local SSD. By restricting the vCPU count while maintaining a high memory capacity of 14.0 GB per vCPU, it optimizes software licensing efficiency for core-bound enterprise applications. In benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers top-tier memory scores in PassMark and strong multi-core throughput in stress-ng and Geekbench. While unaccelerated CPU text generation on large language models is restricted, multithreaded data decompression and encryption performance are strong. This makes the server an effective choice for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput ETL data pipelines, and analytics workloads requiring massive working sets paired with fast local NVMe or SSD storage.
